content.text: Section 22 fully matches the preferred position, and no other audit/inspection right binds us.

input.quote: Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.
input.rationale: Section 22 meets the preferred position on every material term: frequency is capped at once per twelve months (22.1), notice is thirty days' prior written notice, audits occur during normal business hours, off-site where practicable, and by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality. Section 22.2 puts audit costs on Vendor unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent, and expressly bars Vendor and its auditor from accessing Customer systems directly or Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, or other suppliers' confidential information — so the walk-away triggers (unlimited/unannounced audits, remote system access) are absent. Section 22.3 additionally treats findings as Customer Confidential Information and requires the final report to be shared, which favours us. Section 23 (Records and Customer Assurance) is a heading with no substantive text, so it creates no additional audit exposure, and no other clause imposes inspection or verification rights on us. No redline required.
